title: The Observer Effect — Portfolio v3
tagline: Angular 21 · D3 force graph · Three.js icosahedron · NLP toolbar
description: This portfolio — a zoneless Angular 21 application featuring a D3 v7 force-directed career graph, Three.js rotating icosahedron, quantum interference canvas background, and an NLP-powered agentic toolbar. Built with a custom glassmorphism design system, Tailwind v4 CSS-first tokens, and lazy-loaded 7-dimension routing.

title: Qutrit Magic State Distillation Research
tagline: Searching for high-threshold distillation routines for fault-tolerant qutrits
description: Research into magic state distillation for qutrits using self-dual additive codes over GF(9). Developed the algebraic framework connecting classical coding theory to qutrit stabiliser codes, constructed candidate distillation circuits, and identified routines exceeding previously known distillation thresholds. Published as arXiv:2408.00436 and presented as a poster at QIP 2022.

title: QuSudoku — Quantum Sudoku Solver
tagline: iQuHACK 2021 — D-Wave hybrid quantum annealing solves N×N Sudoku as graph coloring
description: Built at MIT's iQuHACK 2021 hackathon (Team Sycamore — Rishabh Singhal, Niranjan P N, Rohit K S S Vuppala). The core insight: N×N Sudoku is NP-complete and maps directly to graph coloring. `graphModelling()` builds a NetworkX graph where each cell is a node and edges encode the three Sudoku constraint classes (same row, same column, same sub-square). `buildDQM()` constructs a `DiscreteQuadraticModel` with one variable per cell (cases = N colors), sets linear biases across all colors, and adds quadratic QUBO penalties (lagrange=1000) for every edge to penalise same-color adjacent cells. Pre-filled cells are fixed by zeroing out conflicting quadratic terms. `solveSudoku()` submits the model to D-Wave's `LeapHybridDQMSampler`, reads the lowest-energy sample, and validates the solution by checking every graph edge for color conflicts. Generalises to any graph coloring problem including wireless frequency assignment.

title: Mock Interview Scheduler
tagline: Full-stack platform — auto-schedules peer mock interviews by availability and skillset
description: Community platform (package `com.example.MockProject`) enabling engineers and students to conduct or appear for mock technical interviews. A Spring MVC REST backend exposes endpoints for user registration, availability slot management, and skill-tag declaration. A scheduling engine matches interviewers and interviewees whose available windows overlap and whose skill tags intersect, eliminating manual coordination over chat or email. A React frontend handles the booking flow, upcoming interview dashboard, and interview feedback forms. Built during June–August 2020 to help job-seekers practice under realistic interview conditions with structured feedback.

title: Covid Reliever
tagline: HACKON 2020 — gamified essentials ordering + mental wellness for lockdown
description: Hackathon project (HACKON 2020) combining essential-goods logistics with mental health support during COVID-19 lockdowns. The Python/Flask backend connects users to nearby grocery stores, chemists, and vegetable vendors; prescription images can be uploaded for medicine orders with home delivery. Alongside the e-commerce surface, a PyGame-powered mini-game asks players to eliminate virus particles while protecting virtual family members — top scorers receive discount vouchers and priority order slots, creating a retention loop that also addresses isolation-driven anxiety. MongoDB stores user profiles, store inventories, order history, and game leaderboards. HTML/CSS templates render the storefront and game wrapper in-browser.

title: Voice Controlled Assistant
tagline: Speech-driven Raspberry Pi assistant — emails, notes, and GPIO control by voice
description: Embedded voice-interface system running on a Raspberry Pi that converts continuous speech input into structured control signals and actions. The pipeline captures audio via a connected microphone, applies keyword-spotting and intent classification using Python speech-recognition libraries, and dispatches corresponding actions: composing and sending voice-generated emails via SMTP, appending timestamped notes to local storage, and driving GPIO-connected peripherals. The system operates offline for local commands and escalates to cloud APIs for open-ended queries, making it robust in low-connectivity IoT environments. Designed as a hands-free control layer for lab equipment and home automation experiments.

title: Multipurpose Mobile Powerhouse
tagline: Solar-powered 160W mobile generator with Bluetooth-commanded Arduino chassis
description: Team hardware project at DEI, Agra (Rishabh Singhal, Harsh Saxena, Umangdeep). A 1m×1m×1.2m aluminium-fabricated vehicle carrying monocrystalline solar panels that generate up to 160W; a relay bank routes output either to a battery pack or direct load. The Arduino Mega firmware listens on the HC-05 Bluetooth serial interface for single-character commands: F/R for forward/reverse motor drive, C/A for clockwise/anticlockwise steering via DPDT relays, T/D/B/E for panel positioning (top, down, back, stop), H for horn, and Q to halt all motion. DPDT and SPDT relay combinations implement directional motor control without an H-bridge IC; a PWM channel governs BLDC speed. State variables track current panel angle to prevent over-travel. The system demonstrates that a compact mobile platform can both generate and consume its own electrical energy.

title: Library Management Software
tagline: PyQt5 desktop app — book catalogue with price lookup and quantity billing
description: Desktop application for managing a library's book inventory, built with PyQt5 and an SQLite backend (`LibraryDatabase.db`). The `GUI.py` module defines a `Ui_Form` PyQt5 widget with three functional methods: `setupUi()` assembles the layout from the Qt Designer `.ui` file, `findprice()` issues a parameterised query to retrieve book metadata and populate the price field, and `findtotal()` computes total = price × quantity and displays the result. `Data Insertion.py` and `Data Retrieval.py` provide standalone scripts for bulk-loading and dumping catalogue records. The entire application ships as a self-contained Python package with no external server dependency — the SQLite file travels with the codebase.

title: Smart Highway — Adaptive Street Lighting
tagline: 4 IR sensors drive a cascading 6-LED window that tracks vehicles to conserve energy
description: Arduino C++ firmware that eliminates the energy waste of uniformly lit, empty roads at night. Four IR proximity sensors (pins 2–5) are placed at fixed intervals; six LED banks (pins 6–11) span the monitored stretch. Each sensor triggers a three-LED window: `prox1` illuminates LED1–LED3, `prox2` illuminates LED2–LED4, `prox3` illuminates LED3–LED5, and `prox4` illuminates LED4–LED6, plus a green indicator. Because consecutive sensor zones share two LEDs, a vehicle travelling through activates a rolling three-lamp spotlight that follows it through the `digitalRead` polling loop. Only the occupied segment and its immediate neighbours are lit at any time; all other banks remain off. The design scales by chaining identical sensor-relay modules along the roadway — no software changes needed for longer deployments.

title: Conflict-Free Graph Coloring Heuristic
tagline: NP-hard coloring approximation — published in Springer + granted patent
description: Designed a novel heuristic for estimating two-colorability for conflict-free coloring in simple graphs. The method uses structural graph properties and greedy exploration to approximate an NP-hard decision problem. Published in Springer's Advances in Intelligent Systems and Computing (DOI: 10.1007/978-981-15-8025-3_33) and granted IP Australia patent 2021104261.

title: Big Data Analysis using Graphlets
tagline: Efficient algorithms for graphlet and orbit enumeration on large networks
description: Research internship at the University of Northern British Columbia (MITACS Globalink) under Prof. Alex Aravind. Studied complex systems using graphlet analysis, designed and analysed efficient algorithms for graphlet and orbit enumeration, and applied them to real-world network datasets. The work involves constructing network graphs from raw data and computing graphlet metrics to extract structural insights.
